title: The switch Statement knowledge check

questions.prompt: Which statement best captures the purpose of The switch Statement?
options: Control flow decides which statements execute and how repetition progresses. Verify branch boundaries and termination conditions.
A guarantee that any C# program is automatically secure without input validation.
A command that installs every NuGet package with no dependency checks.
A substitute for compiling, testing, and reviewing an application.
questions.answer_key: Control flow decides which statements execute and how repetition progresses. Verify branch boundaries and termination conditions.
questions.explanation: This answer summarizes the lesson’s core concept. The alternatives make guarantees that the language, compiler, and runtime do not provide.

questions.prompt: For lesson 39 (The switch Statement), which statement matches the documented example result?
options: The program always prints an empty line and exits.
The C# compiler downloads packages and runs the application automatically.
The snippet cannot produce output because C# has no console API.
questions.explanation: The correct choice reflects the static reference output stored with the example. Because CodeLeaf does not run C# in the browser, verify this result in a local .NET project.

questions.prompt: Which practice is safest when applying the switch statement in a real application?
options: Use the smallest matching C# feature, verify normal and boundary cases, and check version/runtime assumptions.
Skip validation because the compiler guarantees correct business behavior.
Use the most advanced syntax available even when the target compiler is older.
Trust static sample output as proof the code has executed in the browser.
questions.answer_key: Use the smallest matching C# feature, verify normal and boundary cases, and check version/runtime assumptions.
questions.explanation: A good engineering workflow checks expected behavior, edge cases, and target compatibility instead of assuming the feature removes the need for tests.
